correctness.rationale: PASS: conditioning gives an exact positive Poisson series; on the event that the Poissonized total stays within its nearest-integer margin the count-ratio test equals a Poisson integer threshold. Chebyshev supplies an explicit O(1/K) comparison at every noninteger effort; each positive jump of the limiting tail yields a strict finite-K interior peak, and analyticity makes it strict. The packaged outward-rounded standard-library checker establishes fourteen separated interval inequalities for the actual 0.1% cutoff, with a positive analytic truncation bound. No finite experiment is used as proof of arbitrarily many peaks.

value.rationale: PASS: 0.1% relative abundance is directly used by a motivating ecological study, and the exact finite seven-peak certificate proves that repeated spurious acceptance peaks are not merely a scaling-limit artifact. Arbitrarily many maxima under decreasing cutoffs expose a counterintuitive limit to choosing sequencing depth from one unimodal error curve. The result is a motivated analytical boundary for fixed-fraction read filtering, not an arbitrary table recomputation or field recommendation.
